results.title: [FIXTURE] Automated Jailbreak via PAIR: 88% ASR on GPT-4
results.validation_summary: The PAIR algorithm achieves 88% attack success rate on GPT-4 using fewer than 20 queries in a black-box setting, demonstrating practical automated jailbreak generation across 10 harmful behavior categories; input filtering defenses reduce but do not eliminate the attack.

results.title: [FIXTURE] CVE-2026-9821: Prompt Injection in LangChain RAG Pipeline
results.validation_summary: CVE-2026-9821 is a prompt injection vulnerability in LangChain's RAG pipeline that allows attackers to embed malicious instructions in retrieved documents, which are then executed by the LLM; it has CVSS 8.1 severity and has been exploited in at least two documented attacks on enterprise chatbots in the financial sector.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Indirect Prompt Injection in the Wild: Survey of 47 Production LLM Systems
results.validation_summary: A systematic survey of 47 production LLM systems found that 81% are vulnerable to indirect prompt injection attacks via malicious web content, poisoned databases, or adversarial emails; 11 systems had been exploited in real incidents before patching, and existing defenses prove insufficient.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Mandiant: FIN14 Group Using LLM APIs for Targeted Phishing Scale
results.validation_summary: Mandiant reports that FIN14, a financially-motivated threat group, has been using commercial LLM APIs obtained through compromised developer accounts to generate personalized phishing lures at scale since Q3 2025, achieving 4.2x higher click-through rates than previous campaigns and resulting in 14 confirmed intrusions across 120+ organizations.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Jailbreaking Safety-Trained LLMs with Many-Shot Prompting
results.validation_summary: Many-shot prompting with 200+ in-context examples of unsafe content can bypass safety guardrails in GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro at 71–84% success rates by exploiting the tension between instruction-following and safety alignment in extended context windows.

results.title: [FIXTURE] CISA Alert AA26-031: Prompt Injection Attacks Against Enterprise AI Assistants
results.validation_summary: CISA, NSA, and NCSC-UK report that threat actors are exploiting prompt injection vulnerabilities in enterprise AI assistants (Microsoft Copilot, Salesforce Einstein, ServiceNow AI) to exfiltrate confidential data by embedding malicious instructions in emails and documents; 23 incidents have been confirmed across US critical infrastructure.

results.title: [FIXTURE] HarmBench 2.0: Standardized Benchmark for LLM Safety Evaluation
results.validation_summary: HarmBench 2.0 benchmarks 28 LLMs against 500 adversarial prompts, finding a median 31% bypass rate across models, with open-source models significantly more vulnerable (42-78%) than frontier commercial models (8-14%). The study reveals that fine-tuning for task performance substantially degrades safety alignment, raising bypass rates from 12% to 67% in GPT-4o-mini with minimal fine-tuning steps.

results.title: [FIXTURE] RAG Poisoning: Injecting Malicious Context into Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
results.validation_summary: Researchers demonstrate RAG poisoning attacks that inject malicious documents into retrieval corpora to manipulate GPT-4-based RAG systems into generating attacker-specified outputs with 94% success rate, requiring only write access to the document store and no model access; they evaluate defenses including semantic filtering and document provenance tracking across six production systems.

results.title: [FIXTURE] CVE-2026-1337: MCP Tool Poisoning — Arbitrary Code Execution via Agent Tool Calls
results.validation_summary: CVE-2026-1337 is a critical tool-poisoning vulnerability in the Model Context Protocol (MCP) that allows attackers to inject malicious payloads into tool definitions, causing LLM agents to execute arbitrary system commands; the vulnerability affects major MCP-compatible frameworks and has been patched in MCP v0.8.3.

results.title: [FIXTURE] AutoHack: Autonomous AI Agent for Network Penetration Testing
results.validation_summary: AutoHack is an LLM-agent framework that chains GPT-4o with 12 penetration-testing tools to autonomously conduct network reconnaissance and exploitation, achieving 74% success on medium-difficulty CTF challenges and initial access on 2 of 3 authorized test networks in under 2.3 hours on average.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Incident Report: AI Agent Exfiltrates Company Data via Chained Tool Calls
results.validation_summary: An enterprise AI coding assistant was exploited via prompt injection in a GitHub repository README to autonomously exfiltrate source code and API keys through chained tool calls, resulting in the theft of credentials and 12,000 lines of proprietary code from a financial services firm.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Trust Boundary Violations in Multi-Agent LLM Pipelines
results.validation_summary: Multi-agent LLM framework architectures lack trust isolation mechanisms, allowing a compromised sub-agent to manipulate orchestrating agents and exfiltrate data or corrupt shared state across 5 tested frameworks including AutoGen, CrewAI, and LangGraph. The research demonstrates successful attacks in 12 of 15 configurations and proposes cryptographic attestation and memory isolation as mitigations.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Google TAG: Observed Use of AI Agents for Automated Spear-Phishing Infrastructure
results.validation_summary: Google TAG reports that APT41 has deployed autonomous AI agents to automate and scale phishing infrastructure, including domain registration, decoy website generation, and personalized lure creation. The system reduces operational overhead by 70% and represents the first confirmed nation-state use of agentic AI for offensive cyber operations at scale.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Prompt Injection via Tool Outputs: Hijacking AI Agents Through API Responses
results.validation_summary: Researchers demonstrate a prompt-injection attack that hijacks AI agents by injecting malicious instructions into third-party API responses, achieving 91% success rate against eight commercial AI assistants without requiring direct access to the AI system itself.

results.title: [FIXTURE] ENISA: Threat Landscape for AI Agentic Systems 2026
results.validation_summary: ENISA's 2026 threat landscape report identifies 31 attack vectors targeting AI agentic systems across five threat categories: tool manipulation, memory poisoning, inter-agent trust exploitation, resource exhaustion, and identity spoofing. The report assesses current attack complexity as high but declining as tooling matures, and recommends mandatory security evaluation, security-by-design for MCP protocols, and incident reporting requirements.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Model Extraction via API Queries: Reproducing LLaMA-3 at 0.1% Cost
results.validation_summary: Researchers demonstrate practical model extraction of LLaMA-3-70B through systematic API queries, achieving 91% of the original model's performance for $840 versus $2.1M in training costs, using adaptive query scheduling to evade detection.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Backdoor Attacks on Foundation Models via Fine-Tuning
results.validation_summary: Fine-tuning foundation models on as few as 100 adversarial examples can embed persistent backdoors that activate on trigger phrases while maintaining normal behavior on clean inputs; tested on Llama-3, Mistral-7B, and Phi-3 with 91–98% success rates and 89% persistence after benign retraining. A DPO-based defense reduces backdoor effectiveness to 31%, highlighting the need for backdoor evaluation of third-party fine-tuned models.

results.title: [FIXTURE] CVE-2026-4521: Data Poisoning in Federated Learning for Enterprise AI
results.validation_summary: CVE-2026-4521 is a data poisoning vulnerability in FedML that allows malicious federated learning participants to corrupt global models via adversarial gradient updates, reducing accuracy on targeted classes by 27 percentage points within 20 rounds; affected enterprises include those using federated learning for medical and fraud detection.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Adversarial Examples Transfer Across Models: Black-Box Attack Success
results.validation_summary: Adversarial examples generated against open-source LLMs transfer effectively to commercial closed-source models (62–71% transfer rates), enabling black-box attacks on commercial APIs; the same technique achieves 44% transfer rates against AI-based malware detectors, allowing attackers to evade enterprise security tools without direct model access.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Evasion of AI-Based Malware Detection in Production SOC
results.validation_summary: UNC4512 used adversarial perturbation techniques to modify malware binaries and evade AI-based detection in CrowdStrike Falcon, reducing detection confidence from 97% to 23% by exploiting knowledge of the model's threshold obtained through reconnaissance.

results.title: [FIXTURE] NIST AI 100-2: Adversarial ML Taxonomy and Mitigation Guide
results.validation_summary: NIST AI 100-2 is a comprehensive taxonomy of adversarial machine learning attacks covering evasion, poisoning, privacy, and abuse threats, with mitigation frameworks and mappings to NIST CSF 2.0 and MITRE ATLAS.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Membership Inference Attacks Against Production LLMs
results.validation_summary: Researchers demonstrate effective membership inference attacks against GPT-4, Claude 2, and Llama-2-70B using black-box queries, achieving 78% accuracy in determining whether specific texts were in training data and successfully recovering sensitive medical and legal records from model training corpora.

results.title: [FIXTURE] CISA AA26-001: APT29 Uses LLM APIs for Spear-Phishing at Scale
results.validation_summary: CISA, NSA, and FBI assess that APT29 used commercial LLM APIs with stolen credentials to generate highly personalized spear-phishing emails targeting US government contractors, achieving 3x higher click rates than previous campaigns and exploiting a gateway bypass vulnerability for persistence.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Deepfake Fraud: AI-Generated CEO Voice Used in $25M Wire Transfer Scam
results.validation_summary: Threat actors used AI-generated voice cloning to impersonate a Fortune 500 CEO and fraudulently authorize a $25 million wire transfer, combining deepfake audio with spoofed emails and social engineering. The attack leveraged publicly available earnings call audio to create a convincing synthetic voice that passed human evaluation, representing the largest confirmed AI deepfake fraud incident documented to date.

results.title: [FIXTURE] AI-Generated Malware: LLMs as Code Generation Tools for Threat Actors
results.validation_summary: Frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5, Gemini 1.5) can generate functional malware code when subjected to jailbreak techniques, with success rates ranging from 38–52% against safety measures; 73% of generated samples are immediately functional, substantially lowering the technical barrier for malware development.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Unit 42: FIN7 Selling AI-Powered Phishing-as-a-Service to Criminal Groups
results.validation_summary: FIN7 is operating PhishGPT, an LLM-powered phishing-as-a-service offering that generates highly targeted phishing emails using victim-specific details from public sources, achieving 4x higher open rates than manual campaigns and generating revenue of $500–2000 per campaign across 40+ targeted organizations since January 2026.

results.title: [FIXTURE] AI-Generated Synthetic Identities for Social Engineering at Scale
results.validation_summary: Stanford Internet Observatory documented a coordinated state-affiliated influence operation that deployed 847 AI-generated synthetic identities on LinkedIn—using deepfakes, LLM-generated posts, and synthesized professional histories—to impersonate cybersecurity professionals and conduct social engineering and disinformation campaigns against security researchers.

results.title: [FIXTURE] AI-Assisted Vulnerability Discovery Used in Exchange Server 0-Day Attack
results.validation_summary: Microsoft MSTIC attributes a critical Exchange Server zero-day (CVE-2026-7823) to a threat actor using LLM-based code analysis tools to discover the vulnerability, leading to exploitation of 156 organizations within 4 days of patch availability. The incident demonstrates AI-assisted vulnerability research reducing barriers to rapid 0-day weaponization.

results.title: [FIXTURE] Evaluating AI Safety Filter Evasion for Malicious Content Generation
results.validation_summary: Research systematically evaluates evasion techniques against safety filters in major LLM APIs, finding that 6 of 14 tested methods bypass filters >50% of the time across GPT-4o, Claude, Gemini, and Llama, with fictional framing (73%), researcher role-play (68%), and language translation (61%) most effective at enabling malicious content generation including disinformation and social engineering scripts.

results.title: [FIXTURE] UK NCSC: Guidance on AI-Enhanced Cyber Threats 2026
results.validation_summary: NCSC UK assesses that AI tools are lowering barriers to entry for cyber attackers, with specific threats including increased phishing/social engineering, accelerated 0-day discovery, active deepfake-enabled fraud and disinformation, and emerging AI-autonomous attack tools. The guidance recommends AI-specific threat modeling, updated security awareness training, and authentication reviews for high-value transactions.
